clue.text: Bath left running when covering current sporting event

indicators.note: the Bath-plus-left letters are wrapped around the current symbol, so they cover it

parts.note: taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current in physics
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Someone left the bath taps on while an electric current was nearby during a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like an anagram signal but gives ON; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The biathlon is a winter sport combining cross-country skiing and rifle shooting.

clue.text: Wimbledon cut-off points restrict the rest

parts.note: to tie someone down is to restrict them
a break is a rest

explanation.surface: A tennis official limits the players' rest at Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a set level at six games is settled by a short points-based shoot-out game.

clue.text: Ridge takes front off toboggan

indicators.note: the word for the toboggan loses its opening letter, so its front comes off

parts.note: a sledge is a toboggan

explanation.surface: A sledger loses the front of the toboggan on a mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow shelf or ridge projecting from rock.

clue.text: Ridiculous talk was ruined by laughter

parts.note: guff is nonsense or ridiculous talk

indicators.note: the little word was is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speech of nonsense was spoiled by the audience laughing at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Guffaws are loud bursts of laughter.

clue.text: Young fliers make scores under par — about time

indicators.note: the golfing word sits around the time letter, so it is about it

parts.note: in golf an eagle is a hole played two under par

explanation.surface: A golfer finally makes some scores under par.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaglets are baby birds of prey, still learning to fly.

clue.text: Sprinted over, helping an orderly account of events

indicators.note: in a down clue over signals that the sprinting word is turned back to front

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, so sprinted
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Someone dashed across to lend a hand with telling the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is a spoken or written telling of a story in sequence.

clue.text: Rower has to bend

definitions.meaning: the oarsman seated nearest the front of the boat

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the front oarsman in a crew, and to bend forward in respect.

clue.text: One who accepts wagers, with strict rules that is

parts.note: to go by the book is to follow strict rules
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A betting man insists he follows strict rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookie, short for bookmaker, is a person who takes bets.

clue.text: You and I dry leaders of each race, getting damper

parts.note: you and I together are we
TT means teetotal, so not drinking: dry

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words each and race lead them

explanation.surface: Two teetotallers lead a race that is getting rained on.
explanation.definitionFit: Damper means more moist, the comparative of wet.

clue.text: In front by this margin at Newmarket?

definitions.meaning: to be in front is to be leading
horses at Newmarket racecourse win by a head's length, among other margins

explanation.definitionFit: The first sense means leading; the second is a horse's winning distance.

clue.text: Calculate the number sent back to the pavilion

parts.note: a figure is a number
in cricket a batsman who is out returns to the pavilion

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer tallies how many batsmen have been dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The pavilion is the clubhouse at a cricket ground, where dismissed batsmen walk back to.
explanation.definitionFit: To work something out mentally is to calculate it.

clue.text: Perhaps an Arab family will contribute 2000 Guineas, say

parts.note: the Arab is a breed of horse, so an example of one
a race is a family, stock or lineage

explanation.surface: A wealthy Arab family will put up two thousand guineas for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2000 Guineas is a classic flat race at Newmarket; the surface suggests money and a sheikh's family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Two Thousand Guineas is one of Britain's five classic flat races for horses.

clue.text: Foreign soldier in the drink is able to move quickly

indicators.note: the soldier is placed inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
a GI is an American soldier, foreign to a British solver

explanation.surface: An American serviceman who falls into the drink can still move fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble, quick and light in movement.

clue.text: The fruits originally of shooting practice areas

indicators.note: only the original letter of the word of is taken

parts.note: firing ranges are places for shooting practice

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the fruits of target practice come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruits.

clue.text: Flog off suit used at Gleneagles

indicators.note: the word flog goes off, turned wrong, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A man sells off his suit after wearing it at a Scottish hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FLOG to GOLF. Gleneagles is a famous golf resort in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs are the implements players swing on a course like the one at Gleneagles.

clue.text: Team leader's short jump

definitions.meaning: a short form of skipper, a team leader (also the captain in curling or bowls)

explanation.definitionFit: A team captain is called a skip for short, and a skip is a small hop.

clue.text: Spinner might produce one on holiday

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A slow bowler takes a wicket while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler; the on side is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg break is a ball from a slow bowler that turns from the leg side to the off side.

clue.text: Insulating material once seen as finest by old school

parts.note: best means finest
OS is short for old school, as in old school tie

explanation.surface: An old school once judged a building material to be the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos was formerly widely used for fireproof insulation until its health risks were known.

clue.text: High points for a Luxembourg rider

parts.note: L is the international vehicle registration code for Luxembourg
a rider is an addition to a document, like a postscript, PS

explanation.surface: A cyclist from Luxembourg takes on the mountain summits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are Europe's great mountain range, full of peaks.

clue.text: The Home Counties apart from holiday venues on coast

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, SE
aside means apart or to one side

explanation.surface: Apart from the counties around London, holiday resorts lie on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties around London; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the coastal area where people go on beach holidays.

clue.text: Swordsmen run through stolen property dealers

definitions.meaning: fencing is sport swordplay, so its practitioners are swordsmen
a fence is someone who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: sport sword fighters, and receivers of stolen goods.

clue.text: Game of snooker ahead represents a devious plot

parts.note: a frame is a single game in snooker
a player who is up is ahead

explanation.surface: A snooker player leads a frame by a crafty scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame-up is a scheme to make an innocent person look guilty.

clue.text: Steep banks deceive safari leader

parts.note: to bluff is to deceive

indicators.note: only the leading letter of safari is taken

explanation.surface: A safari guide tricks the tourists near the steep banks of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluffs are high steep cliffs or banks, often by a river.

clue.text: Middle of belt, on flat side

indicators.note: the central pair of letters of belt is taken

parts.note: even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Someone fastens a belt round their middle and lies flat on their side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue placement indicator: the first piece sits on top of the second. 'side' means a team, not a flank.
explanation.definitionFit: A side such as a cricket or football team has this many players.

clue.text: Ring back about first of internationals in colour

indicators.note: the turned ring word goes about, that is around, the picked letter
the word for ring is read in reverse

parts.note: to call someone is to ring them

indicators.note: only the first letter of internationals is taken

explanation.surface: Someone phones back about the opening international match's team colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CALL into LLAC, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple shade, named after the flower.

clue.text: Help, competent, is at hand

parts.note: to avail is to help or be of use
able means competent

explanation.surface: Competent help is right here when needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at hand is ready to use, accessible.

clue.text: Valid run

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for genuine or lawful, and a phrase for running off.

clue.text: Expected by many to win approval before rearranged tie

indicators.note: the approval word comes before the scrambled tie letters

parts.note: favour means approval

indicators.note: the letters of tie are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A team's approval rating rises before a replayed cup tie.
explanation.definitionFit: The favourite in a race is the runner most people back to come first.

clue.text: Visitor stumbled on the answer, so to speak

indicators.note: signals that the words are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: to guess is to stumble on the answer by chance

explanation.surface: A visiting solver hit on the solution by luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone who visits or stays at another's home.

clue.text: Heat source is under discussion but only partially

indicators.note: says only part of the phrase before is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A heater is being discussed but only partly approved.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun is the star that warms the earth.

clue.text: Cleans up with monies received in Us from horse races

parts.note: to sweep is to clean up with a brush
in American usage the take is the money received, the takings

explanation.surface: A gambler cleans up on American horse races with his winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake was originally a race in which all the stakes go to the winner's owner.
